# GitHub workflows

- `.github/workflows/test-published-packages.yml` runs weekly (and on demand) against the packages published on nuget.org: `scripts/get-published-version.ps1` resolves the newest version all four packages share, the run checks out that version's release tag, and the tests build with `/p:UsePackedNuGetPackages=true` so they consume the published artifacts. The Threading and Cryptography suites need the `STRONG_NAME_KEY` secret (base64 of the signing key) because the published assemblies grant `InternalsVisibleTo` to a signed test assembly; without it the run narrows to Memory
- `.github/workflows/mono-runtimes.yml` runs the Cryptography suite on Mono runtimes the regular CI never reaches: monthly or on demand (`platforms` input), never on PRs. **s390x** is big-endian and the only place the `!BitConverter.IsLittleEndian` branches execute; **ppc64le** is a little-endian Mono JIT on another backend. All three run the tests through `.github/mono-test-host` (`Program.cs` drives `NUnitTestAssemblyRunner` directly, `create-host.sh` generates the project from a `dotnet new` template): VSTest aborts on ppc64le Mono and cannot host browser-wasm, and NUnitLite always starts a thread. **s390x**/**ppc64le** build the host natively and run it with parallel workers inside `registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/dotnet-100` under QEMU, where it names any test running over 10 minutes; **wasm** runs it on Node.js on the main thread (Mono interpreter, single-threaded). Tests that need in-box algorithms browser-wasm lacks (AES, TripleDES, MD5) skip there through `TestHelpers.AssumeNotBrowser` or an `IsBrowser` registry support check. Every build passes `/p:MonoRuntimeTests=true`, which drops the reference libraries that do not run on Mono (HashifyNET and the two native BLAKE3 packages), and benchmark fixtures are filtered out. The Mono JIT miscompiles carries on field-held state — see `.claude/rules/cryptography.md`
